question: Which of the following is the characteristic of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigid as well as flexible**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Constitution is a blend of rigidity and flexibility. Certain provisions can be amended by a simple majority in Parliament, while others require a more rigorous process.
 
• The process of amendment of the Constitution is laid out in Article 368, which provides for three types of amendments – simple majority, special majority, and special majority with ratification by states.
 
• The flexibility of the Constitution allows it to adapt to changing times and needs, while its rigidity ensures the protection of fundamental principles and values.
 
• This characteristic has allowed the Indian Constitution to remain relevant and functional since its adoption in 1950, despite numerous amendments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smallest constitution:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution is actually one of the longest written constitutions in the world. It originally contained 395 articles in 22 parts and 8 schedules. As of now, it has over 450 articles.
 
 
 
• **Multiple citizenship:**
 
 
• India follows a single citizenship model where a person is recognized as a citizen of India only, irrespective of the state or territory in which they reside. This is unlike countries like the USA which have dual citizenship (federal and state levels).
 
 
 
• **Presidential form of Government:**
 
 
• India has a parliamentary system of government. The President of India is the head of state, while the Prime Minister is the head of government. The President's role is largely ceremonial.
